newsitem.title: FINLAND: Enso sees Holtzmann synergy gains in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Enso sees Holtzmann synergy gains in 1999.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group Enso Oy expects synergy benefits from its acquisition of German paper maker E. Holtzmann & Cie Ab of about 170 million markka per year by 1999, CEO Jukka Harmala said on Monday.
"It has been cautiously calculated that we will achieve (the 170 million markka synergy benefits) in 1999," he told a news conference.

Referring to Enso's acquisition of Finnish state-owned Veitsiluoto Oy in 1995, Harmala said: "We hope the experience we had with Veitsiluoto will repeat itself and that (the synergy benefits) will materialise on an even bigger scale, and faster."

Synergy worth about 20 million markka per year would come from merging business operations, about 50 million markka from logistics and raw materials procurement and about 100 million markka from optimising production and products, Harmala said.
The measures needed to achieve synergy would be "relatively easy" to introduce, he said.
"The synergy benefits will begin to be felt already this year," Harmala said.
